skill.name: testing
skill.description: Guides users on writing and running Deno-focused tests with clear file naming, coverage, and pre-commit checks.
skill.summary: Plan and run focused tests for TypeScript and Deno projects.
skill.author: 5t111111

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Markdown-only testing guide with no executable code, network access, or secret handling. Both static findings are false positives caused by inline Markdown backticks around a file extension and a hardcoded test command.

static_findings.snippet: - Write tests in separate files with the `.test.ts` extension in the same
- Use the command `mise run test` to run all tests in the project

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 16 uses Markdown inline code to describe the .test.ts filename extension. It is documentation text, not Ruby or shell backtick execution.
Line 24 documents the hardcoded project test command mise run test. There is no executable script, interpolation, or user-controlled command construction in the skill file.

content.value_statement: Teams often miss edge cases or use inconsistent test structure. This skill gives direct testing guidance for Deno and TypeScript projects.
actual_capabilities: Recommends Deno's built-in testing framework for project tests.
Guides test file placement beside the code under test.
Specifies the .test.ts filename extension for test files.
Encourages coverage for public functions and methods.
Promotes descriptive test names, edge cases, and error handling.
Identifies mise run test as the project test command.
limitations: Does not provide complete test examples or fixtures.
Assumes the project uses Deno and a mise test task.
Does not configure CI pipelines or coverage tools.
Does not choose between multiple testing frameworks.

use_cases.title: Standardize Unit Tests
use_cases.description: Create a simple project testing convention for file names, placement, and required coverage.

use_cases.title: Review Test Completeness
use_cases.description: Check whether public functions have tests for normal behavior, edge cases, and error handling.

use_cases.title: Prepare Changes for Commit
use_cases.description: Use the documented test command before committing changes to reduce failed checks.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner guidance for adding tests to one file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan tests for this TypeScript file using the testing skill guidance. Focus on public functions and clear test names.

prompt_templates.title: Find Missing Cases
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these existing tests against the testing skill. Identify missing public methods, edge cases, and error handling cases.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Test Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest where test files should live for these source files. Use .test.ts naming and keep each test near the code under test.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release Test Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a focused test checklist for this change. Include required unit coverage, edge cases, error paths, and the final test command.

output_examples.input: I added a public validation function and need testing guidance.
output_examples.output: Place a matching test file beside the source file. Cover accepted input, rejected input, boundary values, and error messages.

output_examples.input: I need to review tests before committing a Deno change.
output_examples.output: Confirm public functions have tests, test names describe behavior, edge cases are covered, and the project test command passes.

output_examples.input: I want a consistent test structure for a small TypeScript module.
output_examples.output: Use nearby test files with the required extension, group cases by public API, and include normal, edge, and failure paths.

best_practices: Keep test files beside the code they verify.
Use descriptive test names that state expected behavior.
Run the project test command before committing changes.
anti_patterns: Testing only the most common successful path.
Using vague test names that hide the expected behavior.
Committing code without running the full project test command.

faq.question: What testing framework does this skill recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends Deno's built-in testing framework for writing and running tests.

faq.question: Where should test files be placed?
faq.answer: Place test files in the same directory as the code being tested.

faq.question: What filename pattern should tests use?
faq.answer: Use the .test.ts extension for test files.

faq.question: What code should receive test coverage?
faq.answer: All public functions and methods should have corresponding tests.

faq.question: Does the skill include full test implementations?
faq.answer: No. It provides testing guidance, not complete generated test suites.

faq.question: What command does it recommend before committing?
faq.answer: It recommends running mise run test before committing code changes.
